route.resolved_source_notes: Interlibrary-loan scan but content is a single patient vignette/case note.

section_summaries.individual_presentation: insidious onset of muscle spasms in the left calf and stiffness in his calf muscles; symptoms increased progressively over three years involving muscles of the arms and legs; spasms and stiffness exacerbated by sudden, rapid body movements and emotional upset; hypertrophy and spasm of the paraspinal muscles; hyperlordosis; marked reduction in spinal mobility; boardlike rigidity of the abdomen; hyperreflexia and fasciculations; limping, guarded gait; sensory examination was normal spasms, rigidity and stiffness of the axial and limb musculature, occasionally worsened spasms and stiffness history of psychological problems
section_summaries.individual_diagnostics: workup performed for various neuromuscular disorders including myotonic dystrophy, fibromyositis, benign cramp and fasciculation syndrome, lipid or glycogen storage disease, McArdle's disease, and chronic lead poisoning; diagnosed as having a personality disorder with somatization Electromyography revealed persistent motor unit activity at rest, particularly of the lower limbs, with inability of paraspinal and limb musculature to relax; stiff-man syndrome was finally diagnosed Electromyography of the involved muscles (usually paraspinal and limb muscles) characteristically reveals persistent involuntary motor unit discharges at rest within ability to relax
section_summaries.individual_treatment: treatment with 50 mg/day of oral diazepam, gradually increased to 60 mg/day syndrome is effectively treated with high doses of oral diazepam Treatment with 50 mg/day of oral diazepam was initiated, then gradually increased to 60 mg/day
section_summaries.individual_outcome: marked improvement with a decrease in muscle spasms and stiffness; spasms and stiffness relieved by additional doses of diazepam; patient remains alert, with no sedation There was marked improvement with a decrease in muscle spasms and stiffness; spasms and stiffness occasionally worsened but were relieved by additional doses of diazepam; patient remains alert, with no sedation These patients can tolerate high doses of the drug without any significant sedation
section_summaries.individual_limitations: Drugs such as quinine, methocarbamol, and phenytoin provided no symptomatic relief Whether such problems are a feature of this syndrome or its basis is not clear
